# `silk/crypto/modular`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Constant-time arithmetic on unsigned integers of up to 8192 bits, and modulo an odd number.

## When to use
Use it to build public-key cryptography that works on large numbers, such as RSA and finite
field Diffie-Hellman. `silk.crypto.rsa` uses it. For a fixed curve, use that curve's module,
such as `silk.crypto.p256`, which is faster.

## Details
A [`Natural`](#Natural) holds a value below 2^8192 in 32-bit words. It also has a length in words, which
[`Natural.fromBytes`](#Natural.impl.fromBytes) takes from the number of input bytes, not from the value. A [`Modulus`](#Modulus)
holds an odd number of 3 or more and the constants for Montgomery multiplication modulo it.

Every operation takes the same time for all values of the same lengths: it has no branch and
no memory access that depends on a value. The time depends only on the word lengths of the
inputs and the bit length of the modulus. [`Modulus.powerPublic`](#Modulus.impl.powerPublic) is the one exception: its
time depends on the exponent, so use it only for a public exponent.

## Errors
- [`ModularError`](#ModularError) for a value that does not fit, a subtraction below zero, or a modulus that is
  even or below 3.

## Gotchas
The operations of a [`Modulus`](#Modulus) need inputs that are less than the modulus. Reduce a value with
[`Modulus.reduce`](#Modulus.impl.reduce) first if it may be larger. The values stay in memory after use; nothing
erases them.

## Examples
### Compute a power modulo a prime
```silk
import silk.core.ownership { Copy }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.crypto.modular { ModularError, Modulus, Natural }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let modulus = match Modulus.make(&Natural.fromU64(1000003)) {
    Result<Modulus, ModularError>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<Modulus, ModularError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  // 2^1000002 is 1 modulo the prime 1000003.
  let result = modulus.power(&Natural.fromU64(2), &Natural.fromU64(1000002))
  let mut bytes: [u8; 4] = [0; 4]
  match result.writeBytes(&mut bytes) {
    Result<(), ModularError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), ModularError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 2
    }
  }
  if bytes[0] != 0 || bytes[1] != 0 || bytes[2] != 0 || bytes[3] != 1 {
    return 3
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Modulus` with `import silk.crypto.modular { Modulus }`.

<a id="Natural"></a>

## `Natural`

```silk
pub struct Natural
```

An unsigned integer below 2^8192 with a length in 32-bit words.

### When to use
Use it for the values of public-key cryptography: keys, messages, and signatures as numbers.

### Details
The length sets how many words the operations read, and so how long they take. It comes from
the size of the input, not from the value: [`Natural.fromBytes`](#Natural.impl.fromBytes) with 256 bytes gives 64 words
even when the value is small. Results of arithmetic have the length that holds any result of
inputs of those lengths.

### Gotchas
It is a fixed-size value of about 1 KiB. Pass it by reference.

<a id="Modulus"></a>

## `Modulus`

```silk
pub struct Modulus
```

An odd modulus of 3 or more, with the constants for Montgomery multiplication modulo it.

### When to use
Make one with [`Modulus.make`](#Modulus.impl.make) for each modulus, such as an RSA modulus, an RSA prime, or a
Diffie-Hellman prime, and keep it for all the operations with that modulus.

### Details
Making a modulus of `k` words computes 2^(64 * `k`) modulo it, which takes about as long as
two multiplications of `k`-word numbers per bit of the modulus. The operations then take
inputs below the modulus and return results below it, with the word length of the modulus.

### Gotchas
It is a fixed-size value of about 2 KiB. Pass it by reference.

<a id="Natural.impl.fromBytes"></a>

### Associated function `fromBytes`

```silk
pub fn fromBytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Natural, ModularError>
```

Returns the big-endian `bytes` as a number with a length of `bytes.length / 4` words,
rounded up.

Leading zero bytes are allowed. The time depends only on `bytes.length`.

#### Errors
- `TooLarge` if the value is 2^8192 or more.

<a id="Natural.impl.writeBytes"></a>

### Method `writeBytes`

```silk
pub fn writeBytes(self: &Natural, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), ModularError>
```

Writes the value big-endian to all of `output`, with leading zero bytes as needed.

The time depends only on `output.length` and the length of the value.

#### Errors
- `TooLarge` if the value does not fit in `output.length` bytes. `output` may then hold part
  of the value.

<a id="Modulus.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(value: &Natural) -> Result<Modulus, ModularError>
```

Returns the modulus `value`, which must be odd and 3 or more.

The word length of the modulus is that of its value without leading zero words, so the time
of this call and of later operations depends on the bit length of the value, but not on its
other bits.

#### Errors
- `InvalidModulus` if `value` is even or below 3.

<a id="Modulus.impl.power"></a>

### Method `power`

```silk
pub fn power(self: &Modulus, base: &Natural, exponent: &Natural) -> Natural
```

Returns `base` to the power `exponent` modulo the modulus. `base` must be less than the
modulus; `exponent` can be any value.

The time depends only on the bit length of the modulus and the length of `exponent`, so the
base and the exponent can be secret. A zero exponent gives 1.

<a id="Modulus.impl.powerPublic"></a>

### Method `powerPublic`

```silk
pub fn powerPublic(self: &Modulus, base: &Natural, exponent: &Natural) -> Natural
```

Returns `base` to the power `exponent` modulo the modulus, faster than [`Modulus.power`](#Modulus.impl.power)
for a short exponent. `base` must be less than the modulus.

#### Gotchas
Its time depends on the bits of `exponent`, so use it only for a public exponent, such as an
RSA public exponent. The time does not depend on `base`.

<a id="Modulus.impl.invertPrime"></a>

### Method `invertPrime`

```silk
pub fn invertPrime(self: &Modulus, value: &Natural) -> Natural
```

Returns the inverse of `value` modulo the modulus, which must be prime: the number that
gives 1 when multiplied by `value`. `value` must be less than the modulus. 0 gives 0.

It computes `value` to the power modulus - 2, in the time of [`Modulus.power`](#Modulus.impl.power).
